what_its_for: Sodium picosulfate is a laxative used to relieve constipation or to clean out your bowel before a medical procedure such as a colonoscopy, surgery, or X-ray. It works by stimulating the muscles in your intestines to move stool along and out of your body.
how_to_take: Take sodium picosulfate exactly as your doctor or pharmacist tells you. It usually comes as a liquid, powder to mix with water, or tablet. If it is a powder, dissolve it completely in a full glass of cool water and drink it all. Drink plenty of clear fluids throughout the day while taking this medicine, as it can cause you to lose fluids. Do not take more than the recommended dose.
dosing: For constipation in adults and children over 10 years: the usual dose is 5 to 10 mg (about 10 to 20 drops of liquid or 1 tablet) taken once at bedtime. For bowel preparation before a procedure: your doctor will give you a specific schedule, often two doses taken several hours apart the day before your procedure. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions for bowel prep doses, as they may differ from the standard constipation dose.
missed_dose: If you are taking this for constipation and miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and carry on as normal. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are using this as a bowel preparation for a procedure and miss a dose, contact your doctor or the hospital right away for advice.
storage: Store sodium picosulfate at room temperature, away from heat and direct sunlight. Keep it out of reach of children. If you have mixed the powder with water, use it straight away and do not store it for later use. Check the expiry date on the packaging and do not use the medicine after that date.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking other laxatives at the same time unless your doctor has told you to. Do not take this medicine if you are dehydrated or have not been drinking enough fluids. Avoid alcohol while taking this medicine, especially during bowel preparation. Do not eat solid foods during your bowel preparation period unless your doctor says it is okay. Be careful driving or using machinery if you feel dizzy or weak, as dehydration can sometimes cause these symptoms.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor or seek medical help straight away if you experience: severe stomach pain or cramps that do not go away, signs of dehydration such as extreme thirst, very dark urine, dizziness, or feeling faint, blood in your stool or black tarry stools, no bowel movement after using this medicine for more than 3 days (for constipation), vomiting that stops you from keeping the bowel prep drink down, signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing, or if you have kidney problems and feel unwell.
when_it_works: For constipation, sodium picosulfate usually works within 10 to 12 hours after you take it. This is why it is often taken at bedtime so that it works by morning. For bowel preparation before a procedure, it starts working within a few hours of taking the first dose and will cause multiple loose bowel movements to completely empty your bowel.
special_populations: Elderly patients should be extra careful to drink plenty of fluids to avoid dehydration. People with kidney or heart problems should speak to their doctor before using this medicine, as fluid and salt changes in the body may be more risky for them. Pregnant or breastfeeding women should consult their doctor before use. Children under 10 years old should only use this medicine under direct medical supervision. People with inflammatory bowel disease, bowel blockage, or severe stomach pain of unknown cause should not take this medicine without speaking to a doctor first.
